title: Static Docs Site: How Everything Connects
concept: A complete human-first walkthrough of how content, validation, layout, and transitions work together

scenarios.name: Complete Visitor Journey
scenarios.description: From typing content on disk to interactive browser reading

scenarios.name: Zero-Loading Navigation
scenarios.description: How React 19 ViewTransitions eliminate loading skeletons

scenarios.name: Content Safety Check
scenarios.description: How Zod prevents broken markdown from ever deploying

nodes.label: 1. Content on Disk
nodes.story: Think of this as your filing cabinet. You write every page as a plain Markdown file on your local drive. There is no external database like MongoDB or PostgreSQL. Your files are your database.

ste100.low: The system stores all content in local markdown files.
ste100.med: Fumadocs reads markdown files from the content directory during build time.
ste100.high: The content engine reads local markdown and MDX files for guides, reference pages, and changelog entries. Content authors write entries in local files without a remote database.

validations: Files must reside in content/ directory
nodes.edgeCases: If a file is saved in the wrong directory, Fumadocs skips it and does not include it in the build.

nodes.label: 2. The Gatekeeper
nodes.story: Before any file is allowed onto the website, this security guard inspects every single field. It checks: Is the file name kebab-case? Is the title present? Are the dates formatted correctly? If one rule fails, it stops the build immediately so broken content never goes live.

ste100.med: Zod checks that all titles, dates, and descriptions follow strict schemas.
ste100.high: The schema validator parses raw frontmatter into typed objects. It confirms kebab-case file names, validates ISO date formats, and verifies that every page has a title and a description.

validations: File name must match kebab-case regex
Page description must not exceed 160 characters
Every page needs a title and a description
nodes.edgeCases: If you misspell a field or forget a required value, the build throws a clear error and prevents deployment.

nodes.label: 3. The In-Memory Brain
nodes.story: Once all files pass inspection, the catalogue memorizes the entire site into computer RAM. It calculates reading times and pre-links 'Previous' and 'Next' buttons for every page. Because everything lives in memory, looking up any page takes 0 milliseconds.

ste100.low: The catalogue stores the validated items in memory.
ste100.med: The catalogue module indexes routes and resolves adjacent pagination links.
ste100.high: The catalogue module compiles all validated records into an in-memory graph. It computes reading times, groups pages by section, and connects previous and next items for instant pagination.

validations: Duplicate slug check across all collections
No circular pagination links on first and last entries
nodes.edgeCases: If two markdown files share the same slug, the catalogue throws a duplicate error to prevent broken links.

nodes.label: 4. Next.js Server Engine
nodes.story: Next.js takes the data from the in-memory brain and turns it into clean, fast HTML before sending it to the visitor. It loads the site fonts, creates search metadata tags, and streams the finished page with maximum speed.

ste100.low: Next.js compiles the route into HTML.
ste100.med: Next.js matches the URL, injects font variables, and streams HTML to the browser.
ste100.high: The Next.js 16 App Router maps the requested URL to Server Components. It generates dynamic metadata, applies the site fonts, and streams pre-rendered HTML to the visitor.

validations: Pre-rendering with zero runtime database queries
nodes.edgeCases: If a visitor types a URL that does not exist, Next.js renders not-found.tsx with a helpful back link.

nodes.label: 5. The 1400px Frame
nodes.story: This is the visual house of your website. It creates the documentation layout: a fixed left sidebar with your navigation, a slim top header, and locks the maximum width to 1400 pixels so the site looks balanced and beautiful on widescreen monitors.

ste100.low: SiteShell frames the page with a sidebar and header.
ste100.med: SiteShell positions the left sidebar and restricts the inner container width.
ste100.high: SiteShell constructs the three-zone documentation layout. It shows a sticky navigation bar on the left and a header at the top. It locks the main container to a maximum width of 1400px.

validations: Maximum inner container width locked to 1400px
Left sidebar hidden on mobile screens to save space
nodes.edgeCases: On mobile phones, the desktop sidebar hides automatically, and a touch-friendly slide-over drawer takes its place.

nodes.label: 6. Zero-Loading Engine
nodes.story: When a visitor clicks from Home to Guides, normal websites flash a white screen or show a spinning loader. This engine uses React 19's native ViewTransition to swap pages instantly and fluidly with zero skeletons and zero delay.

ste100.low: React 19 transitions provide instant page switches.
ste100.med: PageLayout uses React 19 ViewTransition to replace content without skeletons.
ste100.high: PageLayout wraps every page in a React 19 ViewTransition element. When the user navigates, the browser crossfades views smoothly without loading spinners or skeleton placeholder screens.

validations: Zero loading spinners allowed anywhere on the site
nodes.edgeCases: If a visitor has a slower network, the page still switches smoothly because all HTML and assets are pre-rendered.

nodes.label: 7. The Live Compass
nodes.story: As the visitor reads down a long guide, an invisible sensor watches which heading they are looking at. It highlights the exact bullet point in the right rail and quietly updates the URL without refreshing the page.

ste100.low: The right rail tracks the active section as you scroll.
ste100.med: An IntersectionObserver watches headings and highlights the active link.
ste100.high: The right rail navigator uses an IntersectionObserver to monitor section headings during scroll. It updates the active pill indicator and synchronizes the URL hash quietly without refreshing the page.

validations: Headings must contain unique anchor identifiers
Offset calculation must account for the sticky header
nodes.edgeCases: If the user has reduced-motion enabled in their operating system, smooth scrolling switches to instant jumps.

nodes.label: Build Stopped
nodes.story: If a content file breaks a rule, the build stops right here. You get a clear message that names the file and the field, and the broken page never reaches visitors.

ste100.low: The build stops on bad content.
ste100.med: Zod stops the build and shows the file name and the failed field.
ste100.high: The schema validator stops the build process with a non-zero exit code. The error message names the file path, the field, and the expected format.

nodes.edgeCases: The deploy platform keeps the last good version online while you fix the file.
